clue.text: Have a wonderful time as mountaineer?

definitions.text: Have a wonderful time as mountaineer?

parts.words: Have a wonderful time as mountaineer?
parts.note: an idiom for living it up, read literally as a climber reaching the summits

explanation.surface: A climber enjoying himself on the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means to enjoy oneself greatly, often by visiting the liveliest places; the question mark invites the literal reading of a climber touching the tops of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a hugely enjoyable outing, taking in all the best attractions.

clue.text: Not apparent one's next in line

definitions.text: Not apparent one's next in line

parts.words: Not apparent one's next in line
parts.note: a successor who is not the guaranteed 'apparent' one, since a nearer claimant could still be born

explanation.surface: Someone queueing who cannot quite be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: An heir apparent cannot be displaced; the other kind of heir is first in line only until someone with a stronger claim is born, so 'not apparent' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In inheritance law this successor holds first place provisionally, unlike one whose claim is certain.

clue.text: One agrees to come to these school periods

definitions.text: One agrees to come to these
definitions.meaning: to 'come to ...' is to reach agreement
British schools divide the year into three ...

explanation.surface: Agreeing to attend certain lessons at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to terms is an idiom for reaching agreement, and the school year is split into terms of several weeks each.

clue.text: Pig clean? Nonsense!

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a pig could be clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is pigswill, used figuratively for rubbish talk or balderdash.

clue.text: Very saintly, but have position in army

indicators.note: in says the position word goes inside the army word

parts.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
to lie is to be situated or have a position

explanation.surface: A holy figure who holds a rank in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiest is the superlative of holy, so most saintly or pious.

clue.text: Judy's wreath?

definitions.meaning: a circle of flowers or leaves

explanation.surface: Asking whether a wreath belongs to someone called Judy.
explanation.walkthrough: Judy Garland was the American star of The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a ring of flowers hung or worn as decoration, and it was also the film star Judy's surname.

clue.text: Son with lots of pages as escorts

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A boy accompanied by many pageboys acting as his escorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pages' suggests the medieval boy attendants, which fits the squires of the answer, but it means sheets of paper here.
explanation.definitionFit: To squire someone is to accompany or attend them, a verb from the knight's attendant.

clue.text: Keen for advancement, but taken home sick

indicators.note: sick suggests something upset or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambitious person who was taken home ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone eagerly pursuing profit or promotion.

clue.text: Donne, my ancestor, used oddly to be very formal

indicators.note: something used oddly is put to strange use, so these letters are deployed in a new order

explanation.surface: Claiming the poet Donne as an ancestor, used in an odd way to appear grand.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was an English poet of the 1600s.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on etiquette and protocol is to behave very stiffly and correctly.

clue.text: Partisan, but unreliable

definitions.meaning: a guerrilla fighter outside the regular army

explanation.surface: A biased supporter who cannot be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a soldier not in the official forces, such as a guerrilla; as an adjective it means uneven or erratic.

clue.text: Some awful tract from an extremist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dreadful pamphlet written by a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective or noun relates to someone holding extreme views, a hardliner.

clue.text: What it costs to send Gestapo wild

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The price of sending the Nazi secret police into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the charge paid for mailing a letter or parcel.

clue.text: Broadcast chief is a fool

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: The head of a broadcasting company is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a silly, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Child thus given name

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A child named in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male offspring.

clue.text: Catching distance?

parts.note: catching here means catching a sound, the range within which something can be heard

explanation.surface: How far away a ball can be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' suggests a fielder catching a ball; it means catching what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range within which a voice or sound can be heard.

clue.text: River rose in spate — filling this?

definitions.text: River rose in spate — filling this?

indicators.note: a river in spate is in a turbulent flood, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A flooded river rises and fills a storage lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition: a river in flood could fill this water store.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake storing water, often fed by a river.

clue.text: Time to speak out for us

indicators.note: speaking out means the word is pronounced, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is time to voice an opinion on our behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent H makes the period of time sound exactly like the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive determiner means belonging to or relating to us.

clue.text: What's viciously said in row gets contempt

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the noise word

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket

indicators.note: viciously suggests violent treatment, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty words spoken in an argument provoke scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viciously' gives ISDA, an anagram of SAID, which goes inside DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is scorn, the feeling that someone is beneath one's notice.

clue.text: Carp served in cider

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the drink's name

explanation.surface: A fish served cooked in cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like a complaint but is the fish family; the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide, or orfe, is a European freshwater fish belonging to the carp family.

clue.text: No member of old family gets out of bed with a jump

parts.note: to be up is to be out of bed
a start is a sudden jump of surprise

explanation.surface: A nouveau riche person leaps out of bed with a start.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a parvenu, someone newly risen in rank and lacking established lineage.

clue.text: Pardon for little woman keeping home

indicators.note: keeping means the name holds the home word inside it

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A small woman remaining at home is excused.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about four sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders.

clue.text: Current dilapidated state of coalpit

indicators.note: something in a dilapidated state has fallen apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Up-to-date report on the run-down condition of a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to present-day matters of interest.

clue.text: Points to Mediterranean island to hide

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
Crete is a large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Directions to a Mediterranean island where one can hide away.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it somewhere hidden.

clue.text: Adds colour, say, to Surrey town

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a town name pronounced the same

parts.note: to stain something is to add colour to it

explanation.surface: Someone paints a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town on the Thames in Surrey, in the county southwest of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines-upon-Thames is a town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: Companion has a smile of ruefulness

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A friend gives a regretful smile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award, abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or distress at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: Frequently take money from attic

indicators.note: take, with from, says the money letter is removed

parts.note: a loft is an attic
L stands for pound, the British currency, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Money is often taken from the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is an archaic or poetic word for often.

clue.text: It's standard to cut vegetable

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a snip is a small cut

explanation.surface: A standard method of chopping a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Take salt with a single shellfish

parts.note: a salt is a sailor; AB is an able seaman
lone means single or solitary

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: season one shellfish with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is the old word for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea mollusc with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Made to run smoothly, though a little drunk

explanation.surface: Something works smoothly even though someone is tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating machinery helps it run, and well-oiled is slang for tipsy, having drunk enough to loosen up.

clue.text: Presses chains

definitions.meaning: smooths clothes with a hot appliance

explanation.surface: Someone pressing against shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron is to press creases out of fabric, and irons are also fetters for a prisoner's limbs.

clue.text: Carlton to broadcast singer

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer is being broadcast on Carlton TV.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlton was a British commercial television company, which makes 'broadcast' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, or a woman who sings in it.

clue.text: Shopworkers' time off-a midwinter afternoon?

definitions.meaning: the weekday when shops shut at lunchtime, giving staff a half-day
in midwinter darkness falls soon, so the day ends ahead of time

explanation.surface: Shop staff enjoy a half-day off on a dark winter afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: In British towns shops used to close at noon on one weekday each week.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the traditional half-day closing for shops, and a winter day also draws to a premature end as night comes soon.
